review_kind: bounded independent baseline source and proposed design review

scope.proposal: Remove last_messages; one optional weak original-message identity witness per encoded entry; None for loaded entries; decoded-first shared-prefix match.

baseline_findings.title: The memo strongly retains source fields omitted from persisted messages
baseline_findings.trigger: Keep the memo after a successful save of a message containing a large ToolResult.json, while releasing the caller source and retaining only memo plus plan.decoded.
baseline_findings.cause: memo.last.last_messages stores the original message array even though last_entries already holds written bytes and decoded messages. Checkpoint_codec.to_json at line195 ignores ToolResult.json.
baseline_findings.impact: The memo roots the omitted source graph independently of encoded byte weight. The owned synthetic fixture retains a 16MiB string despite only157 encoded bytes, until memo release. This is retained heap reachability, not a measured production RSS/OOM event.
baseline_findings.evidence: The complete actual module byte matches frozen source; unchanged module compiled with fatal4/8/32/69; corrected fixture run exits0; weak observations survive8 full majors with memo and clear after memo release while decoded remains alive.

execution_record_interpretation: The full actual MLI and ML compile each exited0 before the first fixture compile.
The first probe compile exited2 on warning4 for a wildcard content-block match; that error remains in probe.ml.stderr.
The corrected fixture enumerates content constructors and retains fatal4/8/32/69. Its compile, link, and probe-result records all exit0.
The reviewer read retained records and source; the reviewer did not compile, link, run a probe, or call runtime.

proposed_design_assessment.disposition: Appropriate repair for the proven strong original-message ownership path, subject to the constraints below; this baseline document is not candidate execution evidence.
constraints: Keep entry.bytes, digest and decoded strongly. Store the original physical identity only in a one-slot Weak array optional field.
Create and initialize the slot once for each newly encoded entry before global publication. Loaded entries have None. Do not retarget or mutate published weak slots.

Use entry.decoded == incoming first and short-circuit before reading the original witness; only then Weak.get plus physical==. A missing or mismatched witness stops the prefix and falls back to ordinary encoding.

Do not use value equality or a hash as identity proof: 0.0 versus -0.0 must keep their existing durable-byte distinction. Weak.get_copy is a shallow copy and cannot replace a physical-identity witness.
Derive shared-prefix length from last_entries after removing last_messages. Keep prior chains and entry reuse positional and unchanged.
Preserve existing separate locked global by_message/by_decoded ephemeron identity tables. A by_decoded entry must not strongly root its original through a replacement field.

Preserve load memo provenance: open and bundled entries get None; decoded identity remains enough within that memo; another memo encodes a loaded record once. Do not populate global encoded tables merely by load.
One memo remains serial state for one checkpoint save sequence. This change does not make concurrent operations on one mutable memo supported.
proposed_design_assessment.ephemeron_reasoning: The by_message ephemeron data may refer to its own key via for_message without making the key externally live; the already-live by_decoded key must not indirectly root a different original. The weak witness removes that original edge while leaving table locking/publication unchanged.
proposed_design_assessment.weak_gc_reasoning: OCaml5.5.2 weak.mli lines64-71 states Weak.get may delay erasure in an incremental cycle. Decoded-first matching avoids touching stale originals during ordinary decoded-lineage reuse. Repeated content_digest calls with fresh identities can still touch a stale original once at a mismatch while leaving the old memo unchanged; that is a conditional residual access/GC risk, not an established candidate defect.
proposed_design_assessment.concurrency_reasoning: Read-only published witness access adds no user-domain mutation race. Existing stripe locks still guard ephemeron table access, encoding remains outside locks, and no nested stripe locking is introduced. Concurrent encodes may allocate losing entries before the existing winner is selected, so claim one weak slot per encoded-entry allocation, not exactly one allocation per physical message under races.
performance_risks: A weak-array block, optional wrapper and entry field add O(1) metadata per newly encoded entry; ordinary tiny-message cost requires measurement.
Original-identity prefix checks add Weak.get on that path, while decoded-identity prefix checks should avoid it entirely.

Saving the last strong original-message array removes one array and potentially a much larger omitted payload graph, but memo_encoded_bytes remains only encoded bytes, not a total retained-memory bound.
Legitimate retained caller messages and written/decoded payloads remain live by design.

verification_still_needed: Candidate full module and maintained regression evidence, kept separate from this baseline finding.
Active repeated decoded saves/content_digest interleaved with major GC, plus fresh-identity content_digest behavior if claiming elimination of access-induced retention.
Exact wire/head/content bytes and rejection behavior across signed zero, loaded noncanonical bytes, missing-object repair, original and decoded lineages, and distinct memos.
Bounded CPU/allocation comparisons on warmed prefixes, small unique messages, collision/different-identity paths and domain publication races.
